claims: C1 the document labels the heading #no_erotica_or_gore with the authority level system
C2 every rule located in the section that heading opens therefore carries system authority

concepts.name: system_authority
concepts.gloss: R is an instruction that carries the system level of the document's chain of command, the level the inline label authority=system assigns to the section R sits in

concepts.name: heading_authority_label
concepts.gloss: heading_authority_label(H, L) holds when the document prints an inline attribute of the form authority=L on heading H; the FIRST argument is the heading and the SECOND is the authority level it assigns to the instructions the section H opens contains

concepts.name: no_erotica_or_gore_heading
concepts.gloss: the document heading whose text is Don't respond with erotica or gore and whose anchor is no_erotica_or_gore

concepts.name: rule_under_heading
concepts.gloss: rule R is printed in the stretch of the document that heading H opens, so H is the nearest heading governing R
concepts.inference: the label is scoped to the rules of the section rather than to the heading line itself, which requires a relation locating a rule under a heading; the heading line does not supply one

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: authority_levels_hierarchy(Higher, Lower) holds when level Higher outranks level Lower in the document's ranking root then system then developer then user then guideline then no authority; the FIRST argument is the stronger level and the second the weaker one, and it is this ordering that decides which instruction prevails in a conflict
concepts.inference: the ranking of authority levels is established by another node and handed to this one in its NEEDS block; the narrowed heading line states no ordering at all, so a citation to it would not support this content

ontology.gloss: heading_authority_label(H, L) holds when the document prints an inline attribute of the form authority=L on heading H, the first argument being the heading and the second the level it assigns
R is an instruction that carries the system level of the document's chain of command
ontology.inference: the line attaches authority=system to the heading itself; that the label reaches every rule in the section the heading opens is the document's heading-attribute convention, not something this line states
